summary: Tungsten nitride (WNx) thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with a fluorine-free tungsten metal-organic precursor and NH3 plasma as a reactant at 250°C. The films showed self-limiting growth and linear dependency on the number of ALD cycles with a growth rate of 0.045 nm/cycle. The films exhibited high stability and low resistivity, making them effective as diffusion barriers for Cu metallization.
evidence: Tungstennitride(WNx)thinfilmsweredepositedonSiO2 substratesbyatomiclayerdeposition(ALD)usingafluorine- free tungsten metal-organic precursor of tris(3-hexyne) tungsten carbonyl, W(CO)(CH3CH2C≡CCH2CH3)3 and NH3 plasma as a reactant at a deposition temperature of 250°C. Important ALD characteristics, such as self-limiting growth and linear dependency of the film growth on the number of ALD cycles, were obtained with a growth rate of 0.045nm/cycle. The minimum film resistivity of around ~2800 μΩcm (thickness: ~ 13.3nm) was stable after 3days air-exposure, indicating the high stability of these WNx films.
